mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar FEDFUNDS spikes (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting investor optimism about labor market strength.
regime_hint: Steady job growth in expansionary labor market
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day ahead returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during such labor additions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (retail sales) of at least 10% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as a mean-reversion signal.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > -10% in a month then rebounds in the next
failure_condition: Mean-reversion pattern fails to predict positive 20-day returns in > 50% of cases (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) reading below 100 (2017=100) persists for two consecutive months, triggering a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as a supply shock proxy.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative in > 80% of such events (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 5% for the first time in three months, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return as a labor market strength signal.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 5% after a 3-month decline
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market tightening
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive in 60% of such episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% and 5% respectively indicate robust demand, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return through interaction effects.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up ≥ +2% AND RSAFS up ≥ +5% in the same month
failure_condition: Interaction effect rank IC > 0.15 over 60-day horizon (no statistically significant excess returns).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a low-unemployment environment where UNRATE remains below 6% for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive in > 80% of such low-unemployment windows (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of 0.5% or more over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via higher real discounting costs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative in > 70% of such CPI declines (p-value > 0.05).
